name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,357

clue.text: Finish filling crack with it

indicators.note: something filling a gap sits inside it, so one word goes into the middle of another

blocks.note: to have a crack at something is to have a try
a finish is an end

explanation.surface: A DIY instruction to complete filling a crack with some putty-like stuff called 'it'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with it' reads as the filler, but it is the definition: fashionable slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone described as with it is fashionable and up to date, which is exactly what trendy means.

clue.text: Tradesman not entirely concealing Dutch accent

indicators.note: not the entire word means its last letter is dropped
to conceal is to hide something inside, so a letter is wrapped within

blocks.note: a tiler is a tradesman who lays tiles
D is the abbreviation for Dutch

explanation.surface: A workman hiding the fact that he speaks with a Dutch accent.
explanation.walkthrough: TILER loses its R to give TILE, which then holds D.
explanation.definitionFit: The tilde is the wavy diacritical mark placed over letters such as the Spanish n, a kind of accent.

clue.text: Solidarity's leader embraced by distressed seamen all at once

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so only the opening letter is kept
distressed things are disturbed and knocked out of order, so the letters are rearranged
being embraced means being held inside someone's arms, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
Solidarity was the Polish trade union

explanation.surface: Upset sailors close ranks around their union leader, acting together.
explanation.definitionFit: En masse is French borrowed into English meaning in a body, all together at the same time.

clue.text: Pull apart largely depressing books on the French

indicators.note: largely means mostly but not wholly, so the final letter is cut

blocks.note: dismal means gloomy and depressing
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A critic tearing apart some rather gloomy books about the French.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismantle is to take something to pieces, separating its parts.

clue.text: Top general introduced to head of free church

indicators.note: the head is the front, so only the opening letter is taken
being introduced into something puts it inside, between the letters around it

blocks.note: opening letter of free
Robert E. Lee, the Confederate general
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A senior general is presented to the leader of a free church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like an adjective for the general; it is a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleece is a soft zipped jacket or pullover, a top worn on the upper body.

clue.text: Have an inclination to ring rector to find out

indicators.note: to ring something is to encircle it, so one letter is surrounded

blocks.note: to lean is to have an inclination or tendency
R is the abbreviation for rector

explanation.surface: Feeling inclined to telephone the vicar to get some information.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn something is to discover or get to know it, as in finding out the news.

clue.text: Ralph managed without parking close to hospital department entrance

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter for parking is removed
something managed is handled and arranged, so the letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
taken as written; P is the map abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Ralph got through the hospital entrance without needing to park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' reads as a doorway, but it is the verb meaning to charm, stressed on its second syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to captivate or delight them, which is what enthral means.

clue.text: Watch Frank about to turn up something revealing

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: to eye something is to watch it
frank and open both mean candid
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Keep an eye out for Frank, who is about to arrive with a revelation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to turn up' looks like Frank's imminent arrival; 'about' is RE and 'to turn up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye-opener is a surprising discovery that reveals the truth about something.

clue.text: Defect with Miles, Dicky and Henry after start of back-stabbing

indicators.note: the start is the first letter, so only that is kept
dicky is British slang for unsound or faulty, so the letters are disordered

blocks.note: opening letter of back-stabbing
taken as written, to be rearranged
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Office politics: a flaw involving Miles, Dicky and Henry after some back-stabbing started.
explanation.walkthrough: Dicky looks like a third colleague's name; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A blemish is a flaw or mark that spoils the appearance of something, a defect.

clue.text: Hint of residue found on each model bird made of clay

indicators.note: a hint is just a trace, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: EA is the abbreviation for each
opening letter of residue
the Model T was Ford's famous car
a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: Traces of residue on each model bird show it was made from clay.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthen describes pots and objects made of baked clay or earth.

clue.text: Using darts primarily to capture small brown bear

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is kept
capturing something means enclosing it, so the outer letters wrap around the inner ones

blocks.note: with can mean using, as in cut with a knife
S is the abbreviation for small
tan is a light brown colour
opening letter of darts

explanation.surface: Firing darts at a small brown bear to catch it.
explanation.walkthrough: WITH and D together surround S and TAN. 'bear' looks like the animal; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To withstand something is to endure or resist it, the verb sense of bear as in bear the pain.

clue.text: Novel set of beliefs

blocks.note: first meaning: the last completed book by Jane Austen
second meaning: a creed or conviction, as in people of every political stripe

explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective meaning new; it names a particular book.
explanation.definitionFit: Persuasion is a Jane Austen novel, and a persuasion is also a religious or political belief system held by a group.

clue.text: Transported in carriage with tenor from start to finish

indicators.text: with tenor from start to finish
indicators.note: tenor is abbreviated T, and moving it from the start to the finish shifts that opening letter to the end

blocks.note: a trap is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage

explanation.surface: Someone riding in a carriage alongside a tenor for the whole journey.
explanation.walkthrough: TRAP begins with T, the tenor, which moves to the end. 'Transported' looks like being carried along, but it means enraptured.
explanation.definitionFit: To be transported is to be carried away with delight, wholly absorbed, as rapt means.

clue.text: Rent collector's first to quit

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter only

blocks.note: opening letter of collector
to have quit is to have left

explanation.surface: The rent collector is the first to give up the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money paid to a landlord; it is a split, the past of rend.
explanation.definitionFit: A rent is a tear or split in something, and a cleft is a fissure or split.

clue.text: Quite happy to eat at home when exercising self-restraint

indicators.note: eating something takes it inside, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: content means satisfied, quite happy
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: Someone happy to dine in rather than go out, as part of a frugal regime.
explanation.definitionFit: Continent means showing self-restraint, especially in bodily appetites, the opposite of incontinent.

clue.text: Sheik oddly neglected to call about the Spanish mercenary

indicators.note: neglecting the odd-placed letters leaves only the even ones
about means around, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters of Sheik
to ring is to call on the phone
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A sheik ignored a phone call about a Spanish soldier of fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: A hireling is someone who works purely for pay, a mercenary who serves whoever hires them.

clue.text: Call to mind even parts of Greek prayer

indicators.note: the even parts are the letters in second and fourth places

blocks.note: second and fourth letters of Greek
a collect is a short prayer in Christian liturgy, stressed on the first syllable

explanation.surface: Trying to remember even fragments of a prayer in Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: To recollect something is to remember it, to bring it back into the mind.

clue.text: Poor editing spoiled gripping opening of novel

indicators.note: something spoiled is ruined and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged
the opening is the very first letter of the word
gripping something holds it inside, so one letter is enclosed

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
opening letter of novel

explanation.surface: Bad editing ruined what was a gripping start to a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gripping' looks like praise for the opening; it is the instruction to wrap the letters around N.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigent means needy and lacking money or the necessities of life, that is, poor.

clue.text: A disinclination to move in time to cover it up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters read from bottom to top
covering something puts it beneath, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
an era is a period of time
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lazy person who, in time, tries to cover up their reluctance to act.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is a tendency to stay still and do nothing, a reluctance or unwillingness to act or change.

clue.text: Illegal activity of gangster not about revenge at the outset

indicators.note: not means without, so those letters are taken away
the outset is the beginning, so only the opening letter counts

blocks.note: Al Capone was the Chicago gangster
on means about, as in a book on birds
opening letter of revenge

explanation.surface: A gangster's crime that is not about revenge at first.
explanation.walkthrough: CAPONE loses ON to leave CAPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A caper is informal for a crime, especially a robbery or heist, so an illegal activity.

clue.text: All the rage to possess my book about bagpipe music

indicators.note: possessing something means holding it, so one piece goes inside the other
about can mean turned round, so the whole assembly is read backwards

blocks.note: hip means fashionable, all the rage
cor is an exclamation of surprise, like my!
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A fashionable book about bagpipe music that everyone wants to own.
explanation.walkthrough: HIP holds COR and B, giving HICORBP, then the lot is reversed. 'My' is the exclamation, as in 'my, how you've grown'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pibroch is a set of elaborate variations for the Scottish Highland bagpipe, its classical music form.

clue.text: Nettle rash at first seen on priest from the east

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter only
in an across clue reading from the east means right to left

blocks.note: opening letter of rash
Eli was the priest who raised Samuel in the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A nettle rash that first appears on a clergyman from the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nettle' looks like the stinging plant, matching the rash; it is the verb meaning to irritate.
explanation.definitionFit: To nettle someone is to annoy or irritate them, just as to rile means.

clue.text: Successfully manages to secure bolt in steering device

indicators.note: securing something holds it fast within, so one piece is enclosed

blocks.note: to handle a task is to manage it successfully
a bar is a bolt on a door

explanation.surface: Someone manages to fix a bolt into the steering mechanism.
explanation.definitionFit: Handlebars are the bar on a bicycle or motorbike that the rider grips to steer.

clue.text: Heroin discovered by border guard

blocks.note: H is slang for heroin
an edge is a border

explanation.surface: Heroin found by a border guard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'border guard' looks like one official; the phrase splits into wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedge is a safeguard or protection, as in a hedge against inflation; to hedge is to guard against loss.

clue.text: Originally pinched from superb cryptic puzzle

indicators.note: originally means at the beginning, so only the opening letter is taken
taking something from a word means removing it
cryptic means obscure and coded, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: opening letter of pinched
taken as written

explanation.surface: An admiring note that a superb cryptic puzzle was stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: SUPERB without P leaves SUERB to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebus is a puzzle that represents words through pictures, symbols and letters.

clue.text: Protective screen placed in position around most of royal family

indicators.note: turned around means read backwards
most but not all, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: to set something is to place it in position
the Tudors were the English royal house of Henry VIII and Elizabeth I

explanation.surface: A protective barrier erected around most members of the royal family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like it wraps one piece round the other, but it turns SET backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A testudo was a Roman formation of shields locked overhead and round the sides, a protective screen for soldiers.

clue.text: Right to be uncertain about accepting ecologist's earliest fieldwork

indicators.note: the earliest letter is the first one in the word
accepting something takes it in, so a letter is placed inside

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
opening letter of ecologist
to doubt something is to be uncertain about it

explanation.surface: An ecologist rightly doubts whether early fieldwork findings can be trusted.
explanation.walkthrough: R and DOUBT take in E. 'fieldwork' looks like scientific research; it is a military earthwork.
explanation.definitionFit: A redoubt is a temporary fortification built in the field, a type of military earthwork.

clue.text: Bit of hogweed found in uninspiring section of river

indicators.note: a bit is a small piece, here the opening letter alone
something found in another sits inside it

blocks.note: tame means dull and uninspiring
opening letter of hogweed
S is the abbreviation for section

explanation.surface: A sprig of hogweed spotted on a dull stretch of riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thames is the river that flows through London and southern England.

clue.text: Object to revolutionary's restless desires

blocks.note: it is a pronoun standing for an object
Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary, with the possessive s

explanation.surface: Someone objecting to a revolutionary's impatient longings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like the verb to protest; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Itches are restless cravings, as in an itch to travel, uneasy urges for something.
